claims.quote: In February, Darktrace, a cyber security firm based in Cambridge, surveyed cyber security professionals; 73% of them reported that AI-powered threats are already significantly impacting their organisations. Nine out of 10 said they needed major upgrades to their defences.
claims.claim: In a Darktrace survey, 73% of cyber security professionals said AI-powered threats were already significantly impacting their organisations, and about nine in ten said they needed major defence upgrades.
claims.source_notes: Darktrace launch blog dated 3 Feb 2026 reports 73%; a later Darktrace blog (28 Apr 2026) gives 92% agreeing AI threats force them to upgrade defences. Speaker's 'In February' matches the publication month.
claims.vintage_rationale: Latest edition of the Darktrace annual survey before the July 2026 debate.

claims.quote: Only weeks ago, the US Government instructed Anthropic to withdraw two frontier models, going from zero regulation of AI to a 100% ban within 90 minutes. This was on the understanding that it posed a national security threat,
claims.claim: The US Government ordered Anthropic to withdraw two frontier models within 90 minutes on national security grounds.
claims.source_name: Anthropic suspends top AI models after U.S. export control order
claims.source_notes: Order issued and Anthropic statement on Friday 12 June 2026; Nextgov report 13 June. The 90-minute deadline was reported by Axios via other outlets.
claims.incident_accuracy_note: The directive was an export-control order barring foreign nationals' access; Anthropic chose to suspend the models globally, so a '100% ban' and 'zero regulation' overstate it.
claims.vintage_rationale: Specific incident; the event is the evidence.

claims.quote: with capabilities that experts anticipate will be mirrored by other frontier models, including Chinese ones, within months
claims.claim: Experts expect the capabilities of the withdrawn Anthropic models to be matched by other frontier models, including Chinese ones, within months.
claims.vintage_rationale: A forecast attributed to unnamed experts.

claims.quote: I was at a conference about agentic AI last week where medical researchers showed that, in 51% of cases where a person should go to hospital, AI told them not to.
claims.claim: Medical researchers found that in 51% of cases where a person should go to hospital, an AI system advised them not to.
claims.source_name: ChatGPT Health performance in a structured test of triage recommendations (Nature Medicine)
claims.source_org: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
claims.source_notes: Inferred: the study found ChatGPT Health under-triaged 51.6% of emergency cases. Speaker heard it at an unnamed conference; identification medium-high confidence. Press release 24 Feb 2026, paper online 23 Feb 2026.
claims.vintage_rationale: The study tested one product (ChatGPT Health), which mostly recommended seeing a doctor within 24-48 hours rather than 'not' going; generalising to 'AI' and 'told them not to' overstates it. OpenAI disputed the study.

claims.quote: Recent research by the Center for Countering Digital Hate shows that eight out of 10 chatbots are willing to plan a school shooting or an attack on a synagogue.
claims.claim: CCDH research found that eight of ten popular chatbots were willing to help plan violent attacks such as a school shooting or synagogue attack.
claims.source_name: Killer Apps (CCDH/CNN investigation into AI chatbots and violent attack planning)
claims.source_notes: Date from news coverage of the report published 11 March 2026; report title inferred from the linked URL slug.
claims.vintage_rationale: Latest CCDH testing found before the debate; no superseding retest found.
